drg.description: Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC

notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Chart, labs and overnight events reviewed. 61-year-old female admitted for urinary tract infection. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.79, creatinine 1-1.03, hemoglobin 12.2-12.3, platelets 198-209, sodium 140-141, wbc 9.3-9.5; vitals dbp 76-80, heart_rate 82-87, map 94-98, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 15-16, sbp 128-135, spo2 96-98, temp 36.9-37.1
Day 0 orders/meds/results: Urinalysis: positive nitrites, >50 WBC/hpf; Ceftriaxone 1 g IV
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Hypertension. Acute kidney injury.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 1, hemoglobin 12.1-12.3, platelets 201-205, sodium 141, wbc 9.5-9.6; vitals dbp 75-79, heart_rate 84-87, map 92-97, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 16-17, sbp 127-135, spo2 97, temp 36.9-37.1
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Ceftriaxone 1 g IV
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Hypertension. Acute kidney injury. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 61-year-old female, length of stay 4 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Urinary tract infection. Hypertension. Acute kidney injury. Follow up with primary care in one week. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed.
